summary: harness.diagnostic codes are classed control or observability in retention.toml; observability codes go to the node's local observation log, which [observations.otlp] exports, instead of replicating, and control codes replicate as before

replay.detail: New harness.diagnostic writes whose code retention.toml lists in local_codes (render warnings, codex and pi driver failures, Claude channel initialization, receipt and handoff reports, native delivery degraded and recovered, unforwarded messages, checkout and start-revocation notices, provider update available) no longer append replicated claims; each goes to the writing node's local observation log, deduplicated by its idempotency key as before. Every other code, including any code the policy does not name, is still a replicated claim. Claims written by older builds, and by older members after this upgrade, are still received, stored and kept.

schema.detail: retention.toml gains an optional local_codes list per kind, used only by harness.diagnostic. The registry, its digest, /v1/schema and every field are unchanged: harness.diagnostic stays a replicated kind and only the listed codes are routed locally. Render warnings now carry the code render-warning, an existing optional field.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule changes and the rules digest is unchanged; harness.diagnostic still has no drop rule.

compatibility.detail: Step 2c, contract C4 of the claims-store breakup (approved). /v1/claims and st trace show no longer list new observability diagnostics; they are in the local observation log and the OTLP logs of the node that runs the seat, and its conversation timeline still shows them. Control codes, and every reader of them, are unchanged, so an older member sees exactly the control codes it saw before. An older member keeps replicating all its own codes, and a new member stores them as before. No wire or client shape changes.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

manual.detail: No manual step. A node without [observations.otlp] keeps these diagnostics in its local observation log for that log's retention.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting to the previous release writes every code as a replicated claim again. The local rows written meanwhile are not read by the previous release (its codex restart fault then falls back to the exit code, and its timeline omits them) and age out with the local observation log.
